canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_1=(N,\Lambda,L_3,L_4,V,\theta,g,\zeta_m,\zeta_v,\vec{\sigma},Z_{3D}^{\mathrm{tw},0},Z_{2D}^{\mathrm{vtx}})\in\mathcal{O}_{P,1}, where \mathcal{O}_{P,1} is the set of tuples with N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}, \Lambda>0, 0<L_4<L_3, V>0, \theta\in\mathbb{R}, g>0, \zeta_m>0, \zeta_v>0, an (N-1)-component compact scalar \vec{\sigma}, an approximated shift-twisted monopole-gas partition function Z_{3D}^{\mathrm{tw},0}, and a center-vortex gas partition function Z_{2D}^{\mathrm{vtx}}.
canonical_goal.target_object: Prove the target proposition that, for SU(N) Yang-Mills theory with N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}, x_4\sim x_4+L_4, N L_4\Lambda\ll1, x_3\sim x_3+L_3, L_4\ll L_3, and L_3\Lambda\ll1, the approximation obtained by restricting the shift-twisted dual-photon monopole-gas path integral to \vec{\sigma}=\vec{\sigma}^{\,*}_k=(2\pi k/N)\vec{\rho}, k\in\mathbb{Z}_N, gives Z_{3D}^{\mathrm{tw},0}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp[2NVL_3\zeta_m\cos((\theta+2\pi k)/N)], and this expression equals the R^2\times T^2 center-vortex gas Z_{2D}^{\mathrm{vtx}}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp[2V\zeta_v\cos((\theta+2\pi k)/N)] after, and only after within these displayed formulae, the fugacity identification \zeta_v=NL_3\zeta_m.
feasibility_constraints: N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}; \omega=\exp(2\pi i/N); C=\mathrm{diag}(1,\omega,\ldots,\omega^{N-1}); S is the N\times N matrix with entries S_{ij}=\delta_{i+1,j} and indices modulo N, so S C S^{-1}=\omega C.

The coordinate x_4 obeys x_4\sim x_4+L_4 and N L_4\Lambda\ll1; the Wilson loop P_4 is constrained by the added potential \sum_{m=1}^{N-1}J_m|\mathrm{tr}(P_4^m)|^2 with every J_m>0; a gauge representative of the selected vacuum is P_4 proportional to C; the resulting low-energy gauge group is U(1)^{N-1}.

The simple roots of su(N) are \vec{\alpha}_a=\vec e_a-\vec e_{a+1} for a=1,\ldots,N-1 in the subspace of \mathbb{R}^N with coordinate sum zero; the affine root is \vec{\alpha}_N=-\sum_{a=1}^{N-1}\vec{\alpha}_a; the fundamental weights \vec{\mu}_a satisfy \vec{\mu}_a\cdot\vec{\alpha}_b=\delta_{ab}; \vec{\rho}=\sum_{a=1}^{N-1}\vec{\mu}_a.

The dual photon \vec{\sigma} is an (N-1)-component compact scalar with \vec{\sigma}\sim\vec{\sigma}+2\pi\vec{\mu}_a for a=1,\ldots,N-1, and its Abelian field strength is \vec f=(g^2/(4\pi iL_4))*d\vec{\sigma}.

The retained R^3\times S^1 monopole-gas Lagrangian is \mathcal{L}_{3D}=(g^2/(16\pi^2L_4))|d\vec{\sigma}|^2-\sum_{n=1}^{N}2\zeta_m\cos(\vec{\alpha}_n\cdot\vec{\sigma}+\theta/N); equivalently, each monopole insertion of species n contributes \zeta_m\exp(i\vec{\alpha}_n\cdot\vec{\sigma}+i\theta/N) and each antimonopole insertion contributes its complex conjugate.

The coordinate x_3 obeys x_3\sim x_3+L_3 with L_4\ll L_3 and L_3\Lambda\ll1; the imposed boundary condition is \vec{\sigma}(x,x_3+L_3)=S^{-1}\vec{\sigma}(x,x_3), and it maps \exp(i\vec{\alpha}_n\cdot\vec{\sigma}+i\theta/N) to \exp(i\vec{\alpha}_{n+1}\cdot\vec{\sigma}+i\theta/N) with n modulo N.

The constant configurations satisfying the shift-twisted reduction are \vec{\sigma}^{\,*}_k=(2\pi k/N)\vec{\rho} for k\in\mathbb{Z}_N; for every n=1,\ldots,N, including the affine root, \vec{\alpha}_n\cdot\vec{\rho}=1 modulo N, hence \exp(i\vec{\alpha}_n\cdot\vec{\sigma}^{\,*}_k+i\theta/N)=\exp(i(\theta+2\pi k)/N).

The two-dimensional center-vortex gas is defined by vortex and antivortex occupation numbers r,\bar r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}, insertion weights V\zeta_v\exp(i\theta/N) and V\zeta_v\exp(-i\theta/N), and the integer-topological-charge constraint r-\bar r\in N\mathbb{Z}; summing r,\bar r with this constraint gives Z_{2D}^{\mathrm{vtx}}=\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_N}\exp[2V\zeta_v\cos((\theta+2\pi k)/N)].

All equalities between Z_{3D}^{\mathrm{tw},0} and Z_{2D}^{\mathrm{vtx}} are claims about the displayed reduced partition functions: Z_{3D}^{\mathrm{tw},0} is obtained after replacing the full \vec{\sigma} path integral by the finite sum over \vec{\sigma}^{\,*}_k, while Z_{2D}^{\mathrm{vtx}} is obtained by the constrained vortex-antivortex occupation-number sum.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_2=(N,n,x_*,L_3,L_4,g,\vec{\sigma},\vec{\Phi},W(C))\in\mathcal{O}_{P,2}, where \mathcal{O}_{P,2} is the set of tuples with N\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}, n\in\{1,\ldots,N\} modulo N, 0\le x_*<L_3, L_3>0, L_4>0, g>0, an (N-1)-component dual-photon field \vec{\sigma} on \mathbb{R}^2\times S^1, a fixed-x_3 magnetic flux \vec{\Phi}(x_3), and an SU(N) fundamental Wilson loop W(C) for a closed curve C\subset\mathbb{R}^2.
canonical_goal.target_object: Prove the target proposition that a single monopole source of charge \vec{\alpha}_n at (x,x_3)=(0,x_*) in the shift-twisted \mathbb{R}^2\times S^1 dual-photon theory has all three displayed center-vortex criteria: \vec{\sigma}=O(\exp[-2\pi |x|/(NL_3)]) as |x|\to\infty, so the magnetic field is localized within transverse scale NL_3/(2\pi); \vec{\Phi}(x_3)=2\pi\vec{\nu}_n for x_*<x_3<L_3 and \vec{\Phi}(x_3)=2\pi\vec{\nu}_{n+1} for 0\le x_3<x_*; and W(C)=\exp(-2\pi i/N) if the vortex flux pierces a surface bounded by C and W(C)=1 if no such flux pierces that surface.
feasibility_constraints: The coordinate x_3 obeys x_3\sim x_3+L_3; the dual photon obeys \vec{\sigma}(x,x_3+L_3)=S^{-1}\vec{\sigma}(x,x_3); under this condition a source with charge \vec{\alpha}_n at x_3=x_* has covering-space image charges \vec{\alpha}_{n-k} at x_3=x_*+kL_3 for every k\in\mathbb{Z}.

The source equation for the monopole configuration is \nabla^2[(g^2/(4\pi iL_4))\vec{\sigma}]=2\pi\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}\vec{\alpha}_{n-k}\delta(x)\delta(x_3-x_*-kL_3), and the boundary condition at spatial infinity is \vec{\sigma}(x,x_3)\to0 as |x|\to\infty.

Writing x_{3,l}=x_3-x_*-lL_3, a displayed solution is (g^2/(4\pi iL_4))\vec{\sigma}=-(1/2)\sum_{l=0}^{N-1}\vec{\nu}_{n-l}\sum_{k\in\mathbb{Z}}[1/\sqrt{|x|^2+(x_{3,l}-NkL_3)^2}-1/\sqrt{|x|^2+(x_{3,l}-L_3-NkL_3)^2}].
The magnetic flux through the \mathbb{R}^2 plane at fixed x_3 is \vec{\Phi}(x_3)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}d^2x\,(g^2/(4\pi iL_4))\partial_{x_3}\vec{\sigma}(x,x_3).

The SU(N) fundamental Wilson loop on C\subset\mathbb{R}^2 is W(C)=(1/N)\sum_{l=1}^{N}\exp[i\vec{\nu}_l\cdot\int_C\vec a], with \int_C\vec a=\int_{\Sigma}d\vec a=\int_{\Sigma}(g^2/(4\pi iL_4))*d\vec{\sigma} for any surface \Sigma with \partial\Sigma=C.
